intro.heading: The read
intro.body:
Klein Cain rides a **55–38 homecoming win** into its first road district game of 2026 under head coach James Clancy.

Magnolia West is **0–2 in District 15-6A** after a 55–7 loss to Magnolia and a 43–42 heartbreaker at Klein Forest, and Ben McGehee’s Mustangs are searching for their first league win at home.

Cain is 3–0 and averaging **47.3 points**; Dave Campbell’s new computer rankings place Cain **No. 51**, up 32 spots after the Tomball win, and Magnolia West No. 194, with the model favoring Cain **by 22**, the widest margin on Cain’s schedule so far.

VYPE named Klein Cain its **Whataburger Team of the Week**, calling the 55–38 Tomball win “about as big a statement as Klein Cain could make.”

Senior wideout Cooper Karns gave Cain Game Day the locker-room read this week: the key against Magnolia West is "to not get comfortable coming off a big win last week and play with confidence." His take on where this team stands: **"we have a lot more in the tank"** and the Hurricanes are "constantly getting better everyday."

The man carrying the offense kept it simplest of all. Asked what the Hurricanes have to do to walk out of Magnolia West 4–0, senior running back Eyan Johnson, fresh off a **190-yard, five-touchdown** night against Tomball, told Cain Game Day: **"we gotta keep our foot on the gas. We can't get complacent."**

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Hanks directs Cain’s offense with a 134.4 quarterback rating, seven passing touchdowns and 81.3 rushing yards per game through three wins. He threw for 348 yards and four touchdowns against Tomball, and his ability to extend plays keeps the Hurricanes from becoming one-dimensional on the road. His receiver Cooper Karns, asked what has impressed him most through three games, pointed to Hanks' "dawg mentality": "he's a great teammate, leader, and elite athlete."

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson averages 126.3 rushing yards per game with seven total touchdowns. His 190-yard, five-touchdown night against Tomball was the breakout performance of Cain’s district opener and the clearest reason Magnolia West has to sell out against the run. Asked by Cain Game Day what it will take to leave Magnolia West 4–0, Johnson said: "we gotta keep our foot on the gas. We can't get complacent."

players.name: Israel Smith
players.copy: Smith’s 117 receiving yards and touchdown against Tomball pushed him to 66.7 yards per game on the season. When Magnolia West loads the box to slow Johnson, Smith is the receiver most likely to make that strategy expensive.

players.name: Cooper Karns
players.copy: Karns answered two questions for Cain Game Day this week, and his message was pure confidence: don't get comfortable after the Tomball win, because this team has "a lot more in the tank." He also delivered the line of the week on quarterback Jace Hanks — "dawg mentality."

players.name: Gage Jordan
players.copy: Jordan leads the Mustangs at 122 rushing yards per game with eight total touchdowns through four games. He scored twice in the one-point loss at Klein Forest and had six touchdowns in Magnolia West’s 2–0 non-district start, giving the Mustangs their best path to staying in this game.

players.name: Collin May
players.copy: May has six passing touchdowns and a 97.7 quarterback rating while also contributing on the ground. He threw for 213 yards and ran for 35 in the 43–42 loss at Klein Forest, and Magnolia West will need that efficiency again against a Cain defense that has allowed 33 points per game.

players.name: Dawson Campbell
players.copy: Campbell leads Magnolia West at 13.3 tackles per game. Dave Campbell’s Texas Football preseason preview spotlighted the senior safety after an 85-tackle junior season, and he remains the Mustangs’ most reliable defender as they try to slow Cain’s multi-threat offense.

items.title: Win early on the road
items.body: Magnolia West is desperate for its first district win and will feed Gage Jordan until Cain proves it can tackle in space, while linebacker Peyton Bjorgaard (13 tackles, two forced fumbles last week) hunts the ball. An early stop keeps this from becoming the kind of shootout the Mustangs played at Klein Forest.

items.title: Finish drives
items.body: Cain is averaging 47.3 points, but Magnolia West has been in two high-scoring district games already. Red-zone efficiency matters more than empty yardage against a team that lost 43–42 last week.

items.title: Keep the edge
items.body: Tomball’s finish turned chippy and Earl Oguinn Jr. was ejected. On the road, in a stadium that needs a win, penalties and extra curriculars are exactly what Magnolia West wants.

items.title: Don't get comfortable
items.body: Cooper Karns named it as the week's key himself: coming off the 55–38 Tomball win, Cain has to "play with confidence" and keep climbing. "We have a lot more in the tank," the senior wideout said in a message to Cain Game Day, "and we're constantly getting better everyday."

final.headline: Klein Cain Rolls Past Magnolia West, 58–7, to Stay Unbeaten
final.byline: Cain Game Day desk · Updated 10:05 PM CT
final.body:
**Klein Cain Rolls Past Magnolia West, 58–7, to Stay Unbeaten**

CAIN GAME DAY DESK · UPDATED 10:05 PM CT

Klein Cain took control early and never let Magnolia West back in it.

The Hurricanes built a **41–0** halftime lead and rolled to a **58–7** road win Friday at Mustang Stadium, improving to 4–0 overall and 2–0 in District 15-6A. Cain's defense forced turnovers, its offense scored on the ground and through the air, and the Mustangs spent their homecoming night trying to keep up.

A week after beating Tomball 55–38, Cain delivered its most decisive win of the season. Dave Campbell's Texas Football had projected a 22-point Hurricanes victory. Cain won by 51.

**Defense sets the tone**

**Jerod Spraberry (#6)** ended Magnolia West's opening possession with an interception and returned it to the Mustangs' 18-yard line. **Jace Hanks (#9)** finished the short drive with a five-yard touchdown keeper, and **Sage DesAutels (#4)** added the extra point for a 7–0 lead.

The Hurricanes kept the pressure on. After Cain's defense stopped Magnolia West on fourth-and-inches, Hanks found **Cooper Karns (#10)** for a 45-yard touchdown. Karns broke a tackle and took it the rest of the way, putting Cain ahead 14–0.

**Braylon Francis (#20)** helped stretch the lead early in the second quarter. The backup running back followed a long gain along the sideline with a run inside the 3, then finished the drive with a three-yard touchdown.

**Eyan Johnson (#16)** powered the next scoring drive, dragging defenders for roughly 20 yards before Karns added a catch-and-run of about 50. Johnson scored from six yards out to make it 27–0 after a blocked extra point.

Then **Easton Mizell (#47)** delivered the biggest defensive play of the half: a 43-yard interception return for a touchdown. Cain led 34–0 with 4:46 remaining.

The defense gave the offense another possession when a Cain cornerback forced a fumble after a catch. Hanks capped the half with a 30-yard touchdown run, his second rushing score of the night.

At the break, the Hurricanes led 41–0.

**Cain keeps rolling after halftime**

Johnson opened Cain's second-half scoring with a 59-yard touchdown run up the middle. DesAutels added a 29-yard field goal in the third quarter, and **Reggie Yarbough (#15)** intercepted another Magnolia West pass.

**Earl Oguinn Jr. (#1)** broke loose for a 66-yard touchdown run with six seconds left in the third, extending the lead to 58–0.

Magnolia West avoided the shutout with 3:58 remaining when **Madden McGehee** scored on a nine-yard sweep. The Mustangs finished with 138 yards of total offense.

Cain's defensive effort went well beyond the takeaways. **Colton Johnson (#40)** recorded a tackle for loss, and the Hurricanes added sacks and stops behind the line throughout the first half.

**Confidence without complacency**

Before kickoff, senior receiver Cooper Karns told Cain Game Day the Hurricanes needed *"to not get comfortable coming off a big win last week and play with confidence."*

Johnson's message was direct: *"we gotta keep our foot on the gas. We can't get complacent."*

Cain followed through. The Hurricanes entered Friday averaging 47.3 points per game and surpassed that mark while holding Magnolia West to a single late touchdown.

The win was Cain's fifth straight dating back to last season and its third consecutive victory over Magnolia West since the teams became district opponents in 2024.

Next comes a shorter turnaround. The Hurricanes host Klein Collins on Thursday, Oct. 1, at Klein Memorial Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. CT. The Tigers are coming off a Friday win over Klein Forest.
